title: Introduce lint shadow mode and dependency alert gateway
author: Nina Patel
release_notes: Adds a non-blocking 'lint-shadow' CI lane to evaluate proposed lint rule changes and a lightweight dependency-alert gateway that surfaces new vulnerability notices to #deps-alerts and creates Linear cards.
description:
Motivation: New lint rules and dependency alerts keep breaking PRs or creating noise because they are introduced with no opt-in runway. This PR adds two pieces: (1) a lint-shadow CI lane that runs the full lint suite but does not block merges and reports rule violations to a dashboard + PR comment; (2) a dependency-alert gateway that accepts Snyk/OSSF notifications and posts summarized notices to #deps-alerts and creates Linear cards for triage. This allows teams to validate stricter lint policies in a shadowed environment before flipping them on, and to centralize dep alerts for faster response.

What changed (high level):
- New CI workflow .github/workflows/lint-shadow.yml: schedules on PRs and nightly, uploads lint output artifact, posts summary comment. Runs same lint matrix as main lint but uses "shadow" reporter and exit code 0.
- Centralized lint rules in infra/lint/config.yaml and a small runtime that can enable/disable rules per-team (infra/lint/manager.py). Existing repo rules were migrated from scattered package.json/.eslintrc files.
- Dependency alert gateway service under infra/dep-alert/gateway.py: small Flask lambda-compatible endpoint that consumes webhook payloads, filters noise, posts to Slack via tools/slack/post_message.py and creates Linear cards using tools/linear/create_card.sh.
- Tests: added unit tests for rule parsing and gateway filter logic under infra/tests.
- Docs: docs/ci/lint-shadow.md and docs/ops/dep-alerts.md with rollout plan and how to opt-in teams.

Testing and rollout:
- Ran lint-shadow on a selection of active repos for one week; collected violations against a curated rule subset (see docs).
- Gateway was dry-run for 48h with real Snyk feed; false-positive rate measured ~7%.
- Rollout plan: enable lint-shadow by default; after 2 weeks, convert highest-confidence rules to 'blocking' behind a Linear-threaded rollout. Gateway will be enabled in production after another 1-week dry run.

Checklist:
- [x] Add non-blocking lint-shadow workflow
- [x] Centralize lint configs and add manager
- [x] Implement dep-alert gateway with Slack/Linear integrations (dry-run first)
- [x] Add docs and rollout notes
- [x] Unit tests for parsing and filtering

Notes on scope and rationale: The shadow lane is intentionally noisy initially but non-intrusive. Teams can opt to subscribe to reduced noise categories. The gateway keeps the source of truth for alerts out of email, centralizing triage in Linear.
commits: 3 commits: (1) 'ci: add lint-shadow workflow and reporter' — creates new GitHub Actions workflow and reporter; (2) 'infra(lint): centralize rules and add manager' — move configs and add small manager lib + tests; (3) 'infra(dep-alert): gateway + slack/linear hooks + docs' — implement gateway, add dry-run mode and docs.

review_thread:

Samir Gupta: Can we reduce the lint-shadow matrix to only changed packages to cut CI cost?
Nina Patel: Good point — lint-shadow uses a file-changed detector (infra/lint/changed_packages.py) and falls back to full matrix on schedule.
Laura Kim: Suggest adding a short-lived toggle so product teams can opt-out for 72h while migrating.

Elliot Zhang: Verified unit tests and smoke-run on staging; approving.
Samir Gupta: Approved (looks good, re-run CI once more to clear intermittent flake).
ci_checks_summary: Initial run: lint-shadow reported violations (non-blocking) and unit tests passed; second run: full suite passed after minor flake fixes. All mandatory checks: build, unit-tests, lint-shadow, integration-smoke => pass.
notes_for_ops: When enabling gateway in production, provision a webhook secret and set DEP_ALERT_DRY_RUN=false in secrets. Monitor #deps-alerts and Linear queue for incoming cards; rate-limit to 5 cards/minute to avoid burst storms.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noise from lint-shadow may create alert fatigue. Mitigation: non-blocking by default, team opt-out label, rule-level confidence tags, and a dashboard to surface only top-priority violations. Risk: gateway could create many Linear cards. Mitigation: initial dry-run + deduplication logic and rate-limiting implemented.
